prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Purpose: original buildable environment concept art for a premium survival game set in an abandoned, drowned subtropical coastal city several generations after people left. Invent solely from this written description. No photographs, no other game's imagery, no existing franchise designs.
Medium: polished digital PAINTING in stylized realism, high-end game art, confident designed forms, rich tactile materials, believable warm late-afternoon sunlight and cool sky fill in shadows. Handsome, restrained, specific. Not photoreal photography, not cartoon, not loose sketch.
Palm construction: every crown consists of distinct pinnate feather fronds with a visible midrib, many slim leaflets on both sides, a rising arch and drooping tip. Open wedges of sky between fronds; clear radial crown star. Never fan palms, banana leaves, fern blobs or fuzzy green balls. Individual trees vary in age, height, lean, crown fullness, missing fronds and minor scars. All crowns grow radially in 3D and work from every azimuth.
Royal: nearly straight smooth pale grey column, subtle swell below mid-height, taper toward a glossy bright green 1.5–2 m crownshaft, 3–4 m arching fronds, compact elevated crown; mature height 14–20 m, trunk about 0.5 m wide with 0.6 m swell. Coconut: slender grey-brown ringed trunk 9–14 m along its curve, 0.3–0.4 m wide, leaning outward then rising, occasional kink/S curve, broad loose 8–10 m crown of 4–5 m drooping fronds, coconuts and old flower stalks just under crown, 0–3 hanging dead brown fronds. Bases flare gently into very tight low mats of thin roots immediately around the trunk, never sprawling roots, buttresses or root stilts.
Output: one finished PNG, landscape canvas, maximum native resolution available; aim for 3840 x 2160. No watermark or decorative border.
Asset: royal_lineup.png. A side elevation lineup of exactly FOUR complete royal palms, roots to highest frond all inside the frame. Broad warm pale sky backdrop with only a faint hazy horizon, cracked former boulevard pavement and sparse small weeds as a narrow grounding strip. Ground datum shared; the four crowns do not overlap. Use wide enough view to show every frond. One quiet 1.8 m tall adult explorer in neutral clothes stands between trees at the same ground depth, very small relative to the tallest tree. Preserve true ratios: person about one tenth of a 19 m palm.
Left to right four distinct sculptural individuals: R1 a 19 m civic survivor with a nearly vertical 0.5 m pale grey trunk, subtle 0.6 m barrel swell below the midpoint, 1.8 m vivid green crownshaft and a full balanced crown of about 17 live fronds; R2 a 16.5 m tree leaning 5 degrees, noticeably narrower uneven crown of 12 live fronds, one missing sector, one long dead umber lower frond hanging below the shaft, small old dark trunk scar; R3 a 20 m older tall tree with stronger low swell, 14 live fronds with two yellowing lower fronds reaching down past the bottom of its 2 m crownshaft; R4 a 10.5 m young short tree, thinner 0.34 m column and 1.5 m green crownshaft, fresh 12-frond crown with shorter 2.8–3.2 m fronds. Distinct individual silhouettes without looking like different species.
Fronds are feathery and three-dimensional, distinct arches, near and far fronds clearly separable, bright new upward spears and dark outward/downward mature fronds. Trunks are smoothly tapered, only faint fine pale horizontal leaf-scar rings, no coarse coconut bark, no exaggerated bottle bulge. Feet visibly rooted with thin compact root mats hugging pavement cracks. Rich sun/shade on smooth grey bark and glossy green shaft, chunky designed form without noisy stippling. Small unobtrusive labels only underneath the ground: "R1", "R2", "R3", "R4"; label by person "1.8 m". No titles or extra text.
